correctness.summary: Equality in the degree-product and degree-sum chain forces a spanning regular component in which every edge is dominating. The complement is therefore a cluster graph, and regularity forces equal cluster sizes; the converse calculation for balanced complete multipartite graphs is exact.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The full accessible source theorem and its sharpness remark were checked, and exact/synonymous searches found no equality classification. The principal residual risks are unindexed observations in the foundational 2005 booksize paper or the 2001 degree-product spectral-bound paper, neither of which was inspected in full.

value.summary: The result turns a newly stated sharp universal spectral booksize inequality into a complete extremal-structure theorem and makes the divisible Turan equality example unique.

limitations: No stability theorem is proved for near equality.
The statement concerns adjacency spectral radius and ordinary triangle books.
